FieldReady Academy

BICSI Installer 1 (INST1) Study Guide and Practice Tests

INST1 Academy is a free study guide and practice-test course for the BICSI Installer 1 written exam. Fifty-two lessons follow the exam's nine areas from the installer's side of the job: pathways and spaces, bonding, firestop, pulling, termination, testing, and troubleshooting. Ten task labs rehearse the work behind the hands-on exam, a printable INST1 cheat sheet collects the distances, fill rules, pulling limits, and color codes worth memorizing, and every practice test is built from the exam's area weights. Use it as your BICSI Installer 1 study guide and take an INST1 practice test as often as you like, free while the site launches. For anyone starting out who wants a structured cabling certification or a low voltage cabling certification, Installer 1 is the usual first step, and the practice tests here are written in the style of BICSI installer exam questions without reproducing any of them.

How the course works

  1. Cheat sheet. Everything the exam expects you to recall cold, printable.
  2. Starter test. A few questions per exam domain, with a confidence rating on each.
  3. Your tutorial. Lessons chosen from what you missed or guessed, each with a checkpoint and a deeper explanation.
  4. Practice tests and retraining. 50 questions, weighted like the real exam. Every miss is explained and feeds back into your lessons.
  5. 3 of your last 5 at 80%. That unlocks one full-length test on the real exam's clock: 75 questions in 120 minutes, at its real passing score of 75%. Pass it once and you are ready to book.

Questions people ask

How many questions are on the BICSI Installer 1 exam?

The written exam has 75 multiple-choice questions in 2 hours, on a computer at a Pearson test center. Questions test both knowledge and how you apply it. A calculator and a whiteboard are provided, and there are no scheduled breaks.

What is the Installer 1 hands-on exam?

Six tasks done to industry standards, 20 minutes each, graded pass or fail after each task. It is given on the last day of BICSI's Installer 1 class. Fail one task and you may retry it the same day at no cost; fail the same task twice, or two tasks, and you retake the hands-on on another date. You must pass the hands-on before you can take the written exam. This course's labs prepare the knowledge behind those tasks; nothing replaces practice with real tools.

How is the Installer 1 written exam scored?

BICSI sets the passing score through a standard-setting panel of experts and does not publish it. If you fail, you get a report of your performance by topic area, not a score. This course's official-format test asks for 75 percent.

Who can take the Installer 1?

No installation experience is required. BICSI recommends its Installer 1 training class, about 50 hours of independent study, and safety and PPE training. Candidates must be able to tell colors apart, do fine hand work, stand for long periods, climb ladders, and lift and carry up to 50 pounds.

How much does the Installer 1 cost?

The application fee is $335 for BICSI members and $400 for nonmembers, and it covers your first hands-on and first written attempt. A retest is $135 for members and $200 for nonmembers. You have one year from your first hands-on attempt, with a 30-day wait between unsuccessful attempts and 90 days after a third.

Does the Installer 1 renew?

No. Installer 1 is a nonrenewable certificate. The next steps are Installer 2 Copper and Installer 2 Optical Fiber.

Is this course from BICSI?

No. INST1 Academy is an independent course and is not affiliated with or endorsed by BICSI. Its lessons and questions are original and never reproduce exam content.

Do I need tools for the labs?

No. Every lab runs on screen. If you want to do the work by hand, a punch-down tool with a 110 blade, a few Category 6 jacks, some scrap cable, a jacket stripper, plugs and a crimper, a continuity tester, and a label maker cost about $50.

Is the course free?

Yes. The lessons, the labs, the cheat sheet, and unlimited practice tests are free while the site launches.

What is on the Installer 1 INST1 exam?

Field Planning, Implementation, and Design (13%), Pathways and Spaces (31%), Pulling Copper and Fiber Cable (21%), Terminating Copper and Fiber Cable (15%), Testing (6%), Troubleshooting (6%), Retrofits (3%), Integration and Convergence (3%), Codes and Standards (2%). The course's units follow the same domains, and the practice tests draw on the same domain weights.
